question.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$R=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,R-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
R-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & -\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(R-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st column, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(R-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & -\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 4 \\ 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda -4)+2(-2\lambda +7) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -4)+(-4\lambda +14) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +10 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-4{\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda -10 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
